Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council
  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  October 14, 2024
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:10 p.m., on Monday, October 14, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, PÉREZ
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Economic Development Specialist Chew

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Vice Mayor Lee

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIAL

1.  PROCLAMATION – F2M24-3

  Ratified the action of Mayor Pérez in proclaiming October, 2024 as BREAST CANCER
  AWARENESS MONTH in the City of Alhambra. The proclamation was mailed to the American
  Cancer Society.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER emphasized the importance of early
  detection and encouraged federal offices to continue to provide funding for research. She went
  on to commend the Alhambra Police and Fire Departments for their continued support through
  fundraising campaigns. She spoke regarding her personal experience as a breast cancer
  survivor. Mayor PÉREZ thanked Ms. Andrade-Stadler for her sharing her battle and stated
  that she had helped to raise awareness as well as inspire others. She thanked Ms. Andrade-
  Stadler for her advocacy.

PRESENTATIONS

2.  CHAMBER OF COMMERCE UPDATE – F2M21-43

  Alhambra Chamber of Commerce President, Mr. John Bwarie, presented an update for
  Chamber of Commerce activities from April 2024 to September 2024. Mr. Bwarie’s
  1
10-14-24
   presentation focused on business attraction program to bring in new businesses, business
  support and retention program to continue to help existing businesses, and the community
  building and capacity building efforts to support Alhambra as a destination for visitors as well
  as strong and vibrant community.

  Discussion: Council thanked Mr. Bwarie for his report and for the Chamber’s work. Mayor
  PÉREZ requested more information regarding the feedback from potential businesses the
  Chamber has reached out to.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

3.  ORDINANCE ADDING CHAPTER 6.28 TO THE ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE TO
ESTABLISH VACANT PROPERTY REGULATIONS – F2M24-33, O2M24-4841

  Economic Development Specialist Tiffany Chew delivered a staff report and presentation,
  which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. The City Council identified in the 2024 Strategic Plan
  Goal Three: Create a Strong Financial Base and Strong Economic Base (Economic
  Development). One of the goal’s objectives was to develop a program to address vacant
  commercial properties causing poor image. The vacant property regulations were intended to
  ensure vacant commercial properties were maintained and secured and to prevent the
  property from becoming a nuisance to the community. The regulations would require property
  owners to register with the City and pay an annual fee within 30 days after being notified by
  the City, post property management contact information on the property, and follow
  maintenance requirements. These requirements included: Property owner registration
  requirements including contact information of the property owner and/or property management
  company if the property owner is not within 40 miles of Alhambra; Building maintenance
  requirements including graffiti removal, and window cleanliness; Landscaping and irrigation
  plan to ensure the property is maintained free of dry plants and weeds; Fencing requirements
  including installation of fencing materials around the perimeter of the property; and, Security
  requirements including maintaining windows, doors, and other entrances. In addition, the
  regulations would provide additional support by activating vacant ground-floor commercial
  properties with window vinyl decals in the storefront windows. Staff would work with property
  owners to provide design and installation guidance. The window decals would be on the
  storefronts while the buildings remain vacant and/or under construction.

  Public Comment:

  1) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova, noted that the ordinance was a step in the right
  direction, but greater clarification was needed as to the parameters of it as to what qualifies
  as vacant.

  2) Joanna VARGAS, representing the Alhambra Central Business Downtown Association,
  spoke in favor of the ordinance.

  Discussion:  Mayor PÉREZ requested information regarding the enforcement portion of the
  ordinance.

  Vice Mayor LEE and Ms. Chew discussed the annual fee as it related to the Code Enforcement
  administration citation fee, as well as the leasing component of the ordinance and similar
  programs in neighboring cities. Ms. LEE expressed concerns with the timeline of 30 calendar
  days for leasing and discussed her concerns with Community Development Director HO who
  clarified that the 30 days was for the owner to clean up the site upon vacancy rather than the
  timeline to find a new tenant. He further discussed staff’s process of communicating with
  property owners and steps to clean up vacant properties. Ms. LEE and Ms. CHEW also

  2
10-14-24
   discussed the window decals and the number of storefronts and properties that had been
  vacant for extended periods of time.

  City Attorney MONTES clarified for Ms. Pérez that the enforcement portion had been removed
  due to the existing chapters of the Alhambra Municipal Code which provide various
  enforcement options for any violations of the code. Ms. PÉREZ and Mr. MONTES went on to
  discuss enforcement options through Code Enforcement. They also discussed staff’s work to
  determine a fee to register a property as vacant through a resolution, which would be
  presented to Council at a later date. Ms. PÉREZ emphasized the importance of pursuing
  properties which had been vacant for a number of years.

  Councilmember MALONEY and Mr. HO discussed what would constitute a vacant storefront.
  Mr. HO provided an update as to staff’s work with property owners such as the Rioni building
  which was not vacant, but had other issues.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER spoke to the vacancies on Fremont Ave. and Valley
  Blvd., the issues of vacant storefronts, and staff’s hard work on the ordinance. She requested
  more information regarding a vacancy tax at a later date, which Mr. HO confirmed that it would
  have to be considered as a ballot measure.

  Councilmember MAZA discussed the chronically vacant properties with Ms. CHEW as well as
  the active Code Enforcement cases to mitigate vacant properties. Mr. MAZA also supported
  future discussion of a vacancy tax ballot measure.

  Mayor PÉREZ and Mr. HO discussed the response of the business community with the recent
  changes to the zoning code as it may allow new leasing opportunities to property owners. Ms.
  PÉREZ and Mr. HO further discussed outreach to property owners regarding the changes to
  the zoning code.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its first reading the following
  ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M24-4841: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council
  adding Chapter 6.28 - Vacant Property Regulations – to the Alhambra
  Municipal Code to protect public health, safety, and welfare by ensuring that the
  characteristics of the City are preserved

  which ordinance shall return for a second reading and adoption at the next Council
  meeting on October 28, 2024.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

MALONEY:  Councilmember MALONEY left Council Chambers at 6:58 p.m. and returned at 7:00
p.m.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 4 – 21)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 9, 16, 20, and 21, were
considered by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

4.  ACCEPT ZIPBOOKS GRANT: CALIFORNIA STATE LIBRARY FOR BOOK DELIVERY
  AND APPROPRIATE FUNDS – F2M24-18, M2M24-183

  3
10-14-24

  continue the purchasing of physical print and audio books to meet unique patron requests and
  to support book delivery services to home or facility bound Alhambra residents. This program
  aimed to meet immediate patron requests of items the Library does not currently own and
  would enhance access for community members who have limited ability to access the Library’s
  physical building and its collection.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted $4,302 from the California State Library for the
  Zipbooks program; appropriate revenue and expenditure funds in the amount of $4,302;
  authorized the City Manager or designee to sign the grant agreement, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, with the California State Library; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-183)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  ACCEPT GRANT: OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY – PEDESTRIAN AND BICYCLE SAFETY
  PROGRAM – F2M24-18, M2M24-184

  The goal of the Office of Traffic Safety and Pedestrian Bicycle Safety Program was to reduce
  the number of individuals killed or injured from collisions involving pedestrians and bicyclists
  through grant funding for local law enforcement agencies. The Alhambra Police Department
  intended to utilize funding for the FY 2024-2025 Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Program to
  enhance community safety through various educational programs. Such programs and
  services would include classroom education, bicycle rodeos, community events and
  presentations on an overtime basis. Participation in programs such as National Walk to School
  Day, National Bicycle Safety Month, National Pedestrian Safety Month and California’s
  Pedestrian Safety Month. In addition, the Police Department intended to use grant funding to
  purchase bicycle helmets to be distributed to community members at various events
  throughout the grant cycle.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) grant in the
  amount of $35,000; appropriated revenue and expenditure funds in the amount of $35,000;
  authorized the Chief of Police to enter into a contract with the Office of Traffic Safety for grant
  implementation; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action. (M2M24-184)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  RESOLUTION: ACCEPT DEPARTMENT OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE CONTROL
  GRANT – F2M11-40A, R2M24-45, M2M24-185

  Staff requested that the City Council adopt a resolution to accept the award of grant funds in
  the amount of $39,100 from the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC). With the
  4
10-14-24
   assistance of ABC grant funds, the Alhambra Police Department would have the means to
  conduct expert training to assist police officers in the prevention and detection of alcohol sales
  to underage consumers. The grant would also allow the Police Department to conduct
  specialized training for owners, managers, and staff at licensee locations to better inform these
  individuals about ABC regulations and best practice methods. The funds awarded by ABC will
  enhance public awareness of underage drinking and law enforcement efforts being dedicated
  to combat this issue.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council 1) adopted Resolution No. R2M24-45 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra accepting the award of grant funds from
  the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control and authorizing the Chief of Police to execute
  all related agreements with the State in relation thereto to accept the award of grant funds in
  the amount of $39,100 from the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control; 2) appropriated
  $39,100 in revenue and expenditure funds in the 2024-25 Fiscal Year Budget to implement
  grant activities; 3) instructed the City Clerk to send a certified copy of Resolution No. R2M24-
  45 to the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control; and, 4) directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-185)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  APPROVAL OF MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT FOR THE 626 GOLDEN STREETS
  MISSION TO MISSION 2025 EVENT – F2M24-16, M2M24-186

  On July 24, 2024, the City Council approved the intent to participate in the 626 Golden Streets
  Mission to Mission event and authorized the City Manager or designee to execute the
  Memorandum of Understanding. The San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG)
  secured $400,000 in Proposition C funds to host the 626 Golden Streets Mission to Mission
  event, with costs for outreach, pre-event planning, and day of event staging. Programming
  required a set amount of in-kind or local fund match from the participating agencies. The
  SGVCOG and the cities of Alhambra, South Pasadena and San Gabriel partnered to host the
  event as a contiguous open street event on June 22, 2025 from South Pasadena to San
  Gabriel. Alhambra’s in-kind match for the event was $20,000. The in-kind match would be paid
  through staff time, services and City-hosted activities at the Downtown Alhambra hub.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA), subject
  to final language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the San
  Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) and the cities of Alhambra, San Gabriel,
  and South Pasadena to share resources and host the 626 Golden Streets Mission to Mission
  event on June 22, 2025 from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.; authorized the City Manager to execute
  said MOA; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action.
  (M2M24-186)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

 8.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: ENVIRONMENTAL ASBESTOS ABATEMENT AT THE
  SHORB CLINIC – F2M24-21, C2M24-37, M2M24-187

  On May 13, 2024, the City Council awarded a contract to Unlimited Environmental Inc. for the
  abatement of asbestos at the former Alhambra Health Center (Shorb Clinic) in the amount of
  $184,000. There were two change orders to the project. The change orders included: removal
  and disposal of two transite pipes, removal of plaster and red brick to access pipes and re-
  installation of plywood on building windows. The change orders totaled $18,042.16 for a final
  contract amount of $202,042.16 Staff inspected this project, and all work was completed in
  accordance with the City’s requirements and specifications. As such, it was appropriate for
  the City Council to accept this project as complete.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Unlimited Environmental Inc. for the
  abatement of asbestos at the former Alhambra Health Center as complete in the amount of
  $202,042.16; directed the City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with the County of Los
  Angeles for recordation; instructed the Finance Director to release the 5 percent retention 35
  days from the date of recordation if no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-187)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ

 10.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION
  SERVICES FOR THE SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON SIERRA VISTA
AVENUE – F2M24-65, RFP2M24-24

  The Sewer Master Plan identified the Sewer Main Replacement Project on Sierra Vista Avenue
  between Los Higo Street and San Marino Avenue. The existing 8-inch pipe WAS expected to
  be surcharged during existing and ultimate peak wet weather conditions. The Master Plan
  recommended replacement of the existing sewer main with a larger diameter sewer main. As
  part of the City’s ongoing Capital Improvement Program, this project would provide
  engineering design, plans, and preparation of bid specifications for the replacement of
  approximately 1,065 feet of existing 8-inch sewer main with a larger capacity sewer main.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
Professional Engineering Design and Construction Services for the Sewer Main Replacement
Project on Sierra Vista Avenue, with proposals due no later than 4:00 p.m. on November 7, 2027;
and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  AMENDMENT TO AXON ENTERPRISES CONTRACT TO INCLUDE CRADLEPOINT
  MAINTENANCE AND VIRTUAL REALITY TRAINING AIDS – F2M23-6B, C2M23-1,
  M2M24-189

  On January 9, 2023, the Council awarded a contract to Axon Enterprises, Inc. for the Officer
  Safety Plan 7, which integrates in-car mobile audio video system (MAVS), body-worn camera
  (BWC) system, digital evidence management software, and Taser 7 in an amount not to
  exceed $1,031,582 over five years. On September 25, 2023, City Council approved an
  amendment to add Axon Air in the amount of $51,638.30 through October 2028. Staff sought
  to amend the current contract between the City and Axon Enterprises, Inc. to allow for the
  purchase of one-year Cradlepoint maintenance and thirty-eight months of Axon Virtual Reality
  for an increased cost of $75,382.83. The Cradlepoint router was initially purchased with Axon
  Enterprises, Inc. and was necessary to purchase annual maintenance to secure the
  connection between the computers and cameras back to the network. Axon Virtual Reality
  consists of headset hardware and accessories and the interactive headsets display various
  scenarios designed to help train officers in de-escalation tactics. Sourcewell awarded Axon
  Enterprises, Inc. contract #101223-AXN for Cradlepoint maintenance expiring December 15,
  2027, and 092722-AXN for Axon VR training with an expiration date of November 21, 2026.
  Cooperative purchase was allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3).

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council amended the contract with Axon Enterprises, Inc. to
  include one-year Cradlepoint maintenance and thirty-eight months of virtual reality training
  aids in the amount of $75,382.83 for a total amount not to exceed $1,158,603.13, subject to
  final language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney; authorized the Chief of Police
  to execute said agreements; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M24-189)

   Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA

12.  APPROVAL OF FIRST AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT FOR LUNAR NEW YEAR
  FESTIVAL EVENT COORDINATION WITH THE ALHAMBRA CHAMBER OF
  COMMERCE – F2M21-43, C2M23-24, M2M24-190

  The City has contracted with the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce for many years to provide
  promotional services on behalf of the City. On April 24, 2023, the City entered into a two-year
  agreement (Contract No. C2M23-24) with the Chamber of Commerce to support the Alhambra
  business community and encourage partnerships within the community. The terms of Contract
  No. C2M23-24 are such that the fee for services may not exceed $120,000 for each fiscal
  year, a total of $240,000 for Fiscal Years 2023-24 and 2024-25. The Chamber requested
  additional funding of $15,000 to support the 2025 Lunar New Year festival scheduled for
  Sunday, February 9, 2025. The funding request would pay for increased costs of event
  management, compliance and fees. This amendment would result in a new contract not to
  exceed the amount of $135,000 for Fiscal year 2024-25.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to the current contract by and between the
  City of Alhambra and Alhambra Chamber of Commerce (C2M23-24) for Lunar New Year
  Festival event coordination in an amount not to exceed $15,000; appropriate $15,000 to the
  2024-25 Fiscal Year Budget for the execution of this amendment; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-190)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

13.  AWARD CONTRACT: FY 2022-2023 SB1 STREET REHABILITATION PROJECT –
F2M22-39, N2M24-91, C2M24-62, M2M24-191

  The FY 2022-23 SB1 Street Rehabilitation Project was located in the northwest area of the
  City. The project consisted of two distinct areas, including residential streets within the Emery
  Park Hills Historic Neighborhood and several mixed-use streets immediately to the east of the
  neighborhood. In total, there were twenty streets included in this project. The Notice Inviting
  Bids for this Project was authorized by Council on July 22, 2024. On September 19, 2024, the
  City Clerk received eight bids that ranged from $2,042,913.00 to $2,598,712.00. Staff reviewed
  the bids and found the bid received from DASH Construction Company, Inc. in the amount of
  $2,042,913.00 was the lowest responsible bid. DASH Construction Company, Inc. had the
  necessary licenses to complete the work and has conducted similar scale projects in
  surrounding cities.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to DASH Construction Company, Inc. in the amount of

  8
10-14-24
   $2,042,913.00 for the FY 2022-23 SB1 Street Rehabilitation Project; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-191)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

14.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: REPLACEMENT OF THE CHILLER UNIT AT THE
  ALHAMBRA POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M24-66, N2M24-127

  The chiller unit at Alhambra Police Department was an original install when the Police
  Department building was built. In the recent months, the building experienced several Heating,
  Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) related issues that necessitated service calls from
  the HVAC provider. Some repairs were made; however, replacement was recommended for
  the chiller unit due to age. The typical life cycle of a chiller is between 15 to 20 years and the
  unit was already beyond that life cycle. The facilities assessment report identified citywide
  projects for the next 10 years beginning in 2021. The report identified the chiller at the Police
  station to be replaced.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to issue a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  replacement of the chiller unit at Alhambra Police Department; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

15.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF A POLICE PATROL VEHICLE – F2M24-6A,
C2M24-63, M2M24-193

  Currently, the repairs to a damaged police vehicle were beyond the value of the patrol car. As
  a result, staff sought to purchase one police patrol vehicle to replace the totaled vehicle
  through a cooperative purchase agreement. A cooperative purchase is allowable per
  Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On September 15, 2021, Sourcewell opened four
  bids for procuring vehicles, cars, vans, SUVs, and light trucks with related equipment,
  accessories, and services. Sourcewell awarded contract 091521-NAF to National Auto Fleet
  Group on November 4, 2021 - a contract that would not expire until November 8, 2025. Per
  the Sourcewell bid specifications, there is the option of purchasing police vehicles. Staff
  recommended purchasing one police vehicle utilizing this option.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and the City Attorney, to National Auto Fleet Group for the purchase of one
  police patrol vehicle in the amount of $54,352.14; directed the Finance Director to allocate the
  insurance payment of $35,611.88 for the totaled police patrol vehicle to account number
  507.70.2010.90803; allocated $18,740.26 from the equipment fund to cover the remaining cost
  of the purchase; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action. (M2M24-193)

   Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA, PÉREZ

  Absent:  NONE

16.  BUDGET APPROPRIATION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE ASSOCIATES (ESA)
  TO PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL CONSULTING SERVICES TO ASSIST IN MANAGING
  THE IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAMS CONTAINED IN THE 2021-2029 HOUSING
  ELEMENT – F2M24-27, C2M24-43, M2M24-192

  On June 24, 2024, the City Council awarded a contract to ESA for managing the
  implementation programs identified in the Housing Element, through October 31, 2029, with a
  total contract amount not to exceed $2,456,634. Staff had originally budgeted a pro-rata
  amount of $491,327 for the first year as a placeholder but as a result of additional guidance
  from HCD, additional programs were identified to be prioritized to be addressed in the first
  year. As a result, ESA proposed a budget amount of $622,689 for the first year of the contract
  (FY 2024-25). As such, additional appropriation was needed to fully fund the expenses
  anticipated during the first year of the contract. The overall contract price would stay the same.
  Staff recommended a budget appropriation from the general plan restricted funds account.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the process of
  adopting the Housing Element and requested a more open and transparent process so that
  the public could receive information, ask questions, and provide input on the implementation

PRIMA FACIE SPEED LIMITS IN THE CITY – F96-33, F2M14-9, O2M24-4840

  The City of Alhambra’s Public Works Department completed an Engineering and Traffic
  Survey (Speed Survey) for 88 street segments citywide and prepared the City of Alhambra
  2023/2024 Engineering and Traffic Survey, which the City Council approved and adopted at
  its August 26, 2024 meeting. The purpose of an engineering and traffic survey was to establish
  updated speed limits that could be legally enforced using radar at pre-determined locations.
  Engineering and traffic surveys could be an enforceable document for a maximum of 14 years
  as long as there have not been any significant changes in roadway or traffic conditions,
  including, but not limited to, changes in adjoining property or land use, roadway width, or traffic
  volumes (for example a traffic signal, road diet, bike lanes, road widening, etc.). States and
  local agencies should conduct engineering studies at least once every 5, 7 or 14 years, in

  speed limits on segments of their roadways. On September 9, 2024, the City Council adopted

  based upon the 2023/2024 speed survey. At that meeting it was noted that some of the existing
  provisions of Chapter 11.08 appeared to be internally inconsistent. The proposed ordinance
  eliminated the references to prior ordinances and replaces the speed limit tables with lists of

21.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE ADDING CHAPTER 5.92
  TO THE ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH REGULATIONS FOR
  SHORT-TERM RENTALS – F2M18-35, F2M24-33, O2M24-4836

  On August 26, 2024 and September 23, 2024, the City Council considered an amendment to
  the Alhambra Municipal Code to include new regulations for short-term rentals (STRs).
  Following the presentation and public comment, the Council provided additional direction to
  add the following additional regulations: 1) Host: Host would be defined as a natural person or
  persons who are the owner of record on a property as illustrated on a deed or legal document.
  2) Eligibility: Types of dwelling units that were eligible to be used as short-term rentals were
  single family residences, duplexes, condominiums, townhomes and multi-family rental units in
  buildings of less than 5-units total. 3) Building Inspection Report: Inspections for all units were
  not feasible because of the amount of time needed. In lieu of an inspection, a building
  inspection report would be required to be submitted to the City annually to self-certify that the
  unit complies with regulations. Staff would be available to conduct inspections on a case-by-
  case basis. 4) Cap on STR Permits: The City would only issue STR permits up to a maximum
  of 500 active permits at any given time, or such other cap as set by City Council resolution. 5)
  Occupancy Limits: The maximum number of occupants for a short-term rental remained as
  originally proposed because an occupancy limit would be unfeasible on properties with more
  than three bedrooms. The current occupancy limits provided consistency and avoided
  disruption to existing STR operations. 6) Grace Period to Obtain Permits: The grace period to
  obtain a short-term rental permit would begin March 1st. Anticipating, the Ordinance would be
  adopted and go into effect January 1st, outreach efforts would be conducted to ensure that all
  potential applicants are informed about the process and requirements for obtaining the
  necessary STR permit. The STR permit would be set to renew annually from the date that the
  permit was issued. 7) Appeal Process: An appeal process for a short-term rental revocation
  will be heard by the Planning Commission. Essentially, if a Host received 3 violations in a 12-
  12
10-14-24
   month period, their permit would be revoked. The operator could appeal that revocation to the
  Planning Commission. Staff requested that the City Council introduce O2M24-4836 for its
  second reading and adopt the ordinance.
